title: multipart: add robust multipart file parsing, content-type validation, and tool/file payload limits (OpenAI compat)
author: Marco Li
description:
Motivation: Several production incidents and developer feedback highlighted inconsistent multipart handling in the OpenAI compatibility layer: streaming uploads were fragile, content-type sniffing was permissive, and tool/function-calling payloads could cause downstream model servers to receive oversized file blobs. This PR implements a unified approach to multipart parsing, strict content-type validation, explicit file and tool payload size limits, and compatibility behavior to match OpenAI semantics.

What this changes: 1) Multipart parser: add a robust streaming-safe multipart parser (compat/openai/multipart_parser.py) that supports chunked uploads, backpressure, and early rejection for headers that exceed limits. The parser emits file metadata and streams file bodies into temp files or direct pass-through buffers based on size thresholds. 2) Content-type validation: centralize allowed content-types per endpoint and file purpose (attachments, tools, embeddings). Implement stricter sniffing and whitelist enforcement with safe fallback error messages. 3) File limits: enforce per-file and total multipart payload limits configurable by route and customer tier. Limits are enforced early during parse with clear 413 responses and JSON error codes compatible with OpenAI field names. 4) Tool/function-calling integration: when requests include tool invocation metadata and file references, the server checks combined payload size against tool-specific limits and rejects or truncates according to policy. 5) OpenAI compatibility: update the OpenAI compatibility adapter to preserve legacy behaviors where reasonable (error shapes, error codes), while surfacing improved diagnostics in logs for operators. 6) Tests & docs: add unit/integration tests for streaming multipart, content-type edge cases, tool payload scenarios, and update docs/api/file_uploads.md with examples and recommended limits.

Implementation highlights: - Added src/compat/openai/multipart_parser.py with a small streaming finite-state machine; exposes a generator-like API to the request handler. - Added src/server/api/files_handler.py changes: early header validation, limit enforcement hooks, and better content-type errors. - Added src/validators/content_type.py with updated whitelist and helper for sniffing first bytes safely. - Hooked limit configuration into routing layer: config keys for route-level max_file_size, max_total_upload_size, and tool_payload_limits. - Tests in tests/test_multipart_limits.py and tests/test_openai_compat_file_errors.py. - Docs updated and a small migration note for SDKs.

Checklist: - [x] Parser and streaming tests - [x] Content-type whitelist and sniffing tests - [x] Tool payload integration tests - [x] Docs and release notes - [x] Security review (basic)

Behavioral notes: - Default limits: per-file 100MB, total upload 120MB; per-tool limits default 32MB unless overridden by config. - For customers on Dedicated with higher tiers, limits are configurable via the console; Private installs can set env overrides. - Error responses follow OpenAI-compatible shape: {"error":{"message":...,"type":...,"param":...,"code":...}}. We preserve code strings used by prior clients where possible.

Rollout & observability: - Feature gated under runtime flag multipart_strict_validation (enabled for beta + all internal clusters). - Added tracing span tags for parsed_file_count, rejected_reason, and size_bytes. - Added metrics: multipart_parse_errors, multipart_rejections_by_reason, tool_payload_rejections.

Migration notes: SDKs (python/typescript) should not need changes; examples updated in docs. Customers using direct private install that changed defaults will need to review new max limits. If needed, support ticket SUP-1782 can assist with per-customer relaxations.

Related: references ENG-2345 (multipart stability), ENG-2399 (tooling payload limits).

centralize content-type validation and sniffing helpers
enforce file and total multipart limits in request handler
integrate tool payload size checks into OpenAI compat adapter
add integration tests and docs updates
review_comments: Evelyn Porter: Nice work on the streaming FSM — a couple of nits: can we reduce memory pressure on the small-buffer path? Suggest using a pooling allocator for temp buffers.
Marco Li: Thanks — addressed by switching small buffers to a shared pool and added a test for buffer reuse.
Samira Gupta: Security question — how do we ensure content-type sniffing cannot be exploited to bypass restrictions (e.g., crafted headers)?
Marco Li: Sniffing is limited to first 512 bytes and done in-memory; we also validate the Content-Type header and apply whitelist. Added tests for obvious header-smuggling attempts.
James O'Neill: Approve after CI fixes. One comment: the error message for exceeding tool payload is user-visible, can we make it more action-oriented (e.g., include current limit)?
Marco Li: Updated message to include current effective limit and added docs example.
ci_checks: ci/e2e: flaky on first run, re-run succeeded
release_notes: Improved multipart file handling: streaming-safe parser, stricter content-type validation, default per-file limit 100MB, per-tool payload guardrails (default 32MB), OpenAI-compat error shapes preserved. Configurable limits for Dedicated/Private deployments.
notes_for_sre: Monitor multipart_rejections_by_reason and multipart_parse_errors after rollout. Watch for regression in latency on small-file common paths; buffer pooling added to mitigate. If customers report false-positives for content-type validation, collect sample headers and open a support ticket referencing SUP-1782.

review_summary: All reviewers approved after two iterations. CI passed on the final run and the PR was squashed and merged. No breaking changes expected; feature is behind a flag and limits are configurable.
